title: Law of averages
statement:
A fair die is rolled $n$ times and you record the proportion of sixes. Which statement is true?

[_]{a}

choices: After a run of non-sixes, a six becomes more likely
The proportion stays the same for every n
After 6 rolls the proportion is exactly 1/6
As $n$ grows, the proportion of sixes tends to get closer to 1/6
explanations: Rolls are independent; the die has no memory.
Small n gives very bumpy proportions.
Six rolls can easily give zero or three sixes.
Correct: that is the law of averages.

hints: The law of averages is about the long run.
solution: With many independent repetitions the empirical proportion approaches the probability, 1/6. It says nothing about short runs.
